observation.what_happens: A green block hangs from a vertical spring fixed to a support at the top. It rises slightly from its initial stretched position and then undergoes small vertical oscillation about equilibrium.

reasoning: Path is a straight line with x near zero and s swinging between ~30 and ~165 px with period ~1.6 s and shrinking amplitude toward ~90 px, consistent with a vertical spring-mass oscillating about equilibrium. Candidates go from ideal simple harmonic motion to linear viscous damping in air to combined linear plus quadratic air drag.

critique.finding: The block bounces around rest level {s_eq} while light friction {gamma} drains the swing. It only partly captures the motion, leaving a steady wobble in the misses.
critique.headline: Hanging block bounces on spring with gentle friction
critique.revision_idea: Add dry Coulomb friction or a small cubic stiffening to the spring. The viscous-only misses swing regularly from side to side with long same-sign stretches, showing energy loss and timing depend on amplitude, not just speed.
critique.why_it_won: It follows the back-and-forth bounce while the falling laws dive away and the ideal spring never loses height.

headline: A law drawn by public randomness, its round named before it existed: a lopsided spring with dry friction and a slow drive. Missed: the misses peaked near the drive's frequency, but Muse Wonder took it for the spring's own.

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6605125). The round was named in 493e869 and pushed before it existed; the law's SHA-256 was pushed in 8337791 before the clip was rendered; the run used commit edb5c02 on a clean tree; the law was revealed in 3636e41. Missed. The drawn law was a lopsided spring with dry (Coulomb) friction and a periodic drive at 4.25 rad/s, slower than the spring's 7.59. Muse Spark's viscous spring won; its damping, 0.74 ± 0.49 1/s, is within 2σ of zero, so its term set is a bare linear spring. The residual spectrum Muse Wonder read peaked at 4.01 rad/s (187 times the noise), 6% from the drive, but Muse Wonder read it as a lower natural frequency: its second try held the spring near 4 rad/s. No model wrote a drive term, and the winner misses the unseen frames by 129 times the noise. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

drawn.equation: x'' = -(k/m) x - (k2/m) x^2 - mu sign(x') + F0 cos(wd t)
drawn.x: displacement below the resting point (m, down positive); t from release

k2.rule: k2 A / k uniform in [0.2, 0.45], stiffer stretched (drawn 0.319)

mu.rule: the swing dies in N half cycles, N uniform in [10, 16] (drawn 15.96); mu = w0^2 A / (2N)

F0.rule: F0 / |w0^2 - wd^2| = share of A uniform in [0.15, 0.35] (drawn 0.295)

wd.rule: wd / w0 uniform in [0.55, 0.8] or [1.25, 1.6], each half the time (drawn 0.560)

sealed.rule: found only if the winner's term set equals the drawn term set, a fitted term whose constant is within 2σ of zero counting as absent, and every shared constant is within 2σ of the drawn value
sealed.terms: winner: linear (ω₀), viscous γ = 0.74 ± 0.49 (1.5σ, absent); drawn: linear, quadratic (lopsided), Coulomb, drive. Term sets differ.
